title: Staples Canada says Staples Print website was breached; contact data and encrypted passwords accessed
date_note: CP24 says the site was hacked between 1 and 5 November and customers were notified on 20 November; the date is the notification day.
geo_basis: country only; the article names a Staples Canada website and gives no city
summary: A Staples spokesperson said its Staples Print website was breached during the first week of November, CP24 reports; the site was hacked between 1 and 5 November and customers were notified on 20 November. Accessed data included contact information, order summaries and encrypted passwords, CP24 reports. Staples said in a statement to CTV News that it has no indication financial information was accessed. Tech analyst Carmi Levy, an affected customer, called the response inadequate.
plain: Staples Canada says hackers got into its Staples Print website in early November and accessed customers' contact details, order summaries and encrypted passwords. Customers were told on 20 November.
exec: A retailer's print-ordering site exposed customer contact data and encrypted passwords; customers were notified on 20 November after a 1 to 5 November intrusion.
action: Staples Print customers: as the Staples email received by analyst Carmi Levy recommended, change your password on the site and watch for suspicious emails.

evidence.quote: The site was hacked between Nov. 1 and Nov. 5 but customers were notified almost two weeks later, on Nov. 20.

validation.note: Single publisher read (CP24), relaying a Staples spokesperson's statement. The Canadian Press article on CTV News (21 Nov) loaded without its body; no Staples notice found on staples.ca.

review.note: stronger than the source: 'no financial data exposed' was CP24's paraphrase; now Staples' own 'no indication' statement to CTV; action advice now attributed to the email analyst Carmi Levy received, not Staples' email to all customers
